purpose: make sure data can be restored when needed, by taking backups on schedule and proving they restore
entry_criteria: Data stores and their recovery objectives are listed
Backup tooling and storage are available
Retention and encryption requirements are known
inputs: list of data stores and criticality
procedure: Configure backups per data store to meet the recovery point objective; encrypt them and store a copy in a separate failure domain.
Monitor each backup job and alert on failure or missing runs.
Restore a recent backup into an isolated environment on a schedule and verify the data.
Record restore time and compare it with the recovery time objective.
Enforce retention and deletion rules, including legal and privacy requirements.
Report failures and restore-test results to the data owner.
acceptance_criteria: Every critical store has a backup that meets the recovery point objective
A restore test succeeded within the recovery time objective
Backups are encrypted and stored in a separate failure domain
validation_method: Database administrator and data owner review of restore results.

validation.check: restore last night's backup into an isolated environment and run row-count and integrity checks
validation.expect: restore succeeded; time recorded; checks pass

validation.check: list backup jobs that did not run in the last 7 days
validation.expect: none, or each has a ticket

failure_modes.mode: Backups in the same failure domain
failure_modes.detection: Copy only in the primary region or account

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A monthly restore of the orders database into a sandbox takes 22 minutes against a 60-minute objective, and checksums of key tables match production at the backup time.
